Ratusan keluarga kehilangan tempat tinggal dalam sekejap. Hasilnya: lebih dari 160 orang dilaporkan meninggal dunia, dan 700 lainnya masih hilang hingga kini. More than 1,300 people are missing in Nepal and Tibet, including 47 Americans, after a glacial collapse caused catastrophic floods, with video showing mud sweeping through entire communities. Drone footage in Nepal showed roads destroyed and buildings buried by thundering water the color of wet cement. Nepalese authorities ramped up operations in the worst-affected districts of Nuwakot and Rasuwa. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet is not a one-off. The Lhende Khola river system has now flooded twice in just 14 months and the increasingly unstable Himalayan ice system threatens communities, infrastructure and water supplies across one of the world’s most densely populated regions. The region saw similar flash floods in August last year, when a glacial lake in Tibet overflowed because of high temperatures. Nine people were killed, and critical infrastructure, including a bridge connecting Nepal and China, was damaged.

Experts say rising temperatures and melting glaciers likely played a role in the collapse. Nepal produces just 0.1% of global emissions. In 2024, it was ranked the sixth most climate-affected country on Earth. Research from Oxfam and the CARE Climate Justice Centre shows that rich countries are profiting from the climate crisis. Nearly 70% of climate finance for the Global South is disbursed as loans rather than grants, and developing countries are now paying more to wealthy nations than they receive.
